dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: I'm looking for a memoir that fits within my budget of $15 to $30. I'm particularly interested in books with high ratings and plenty of reviews. Can you show me some options that match these criteria?
dialogue.agent:
Here are some memoirs that might interest you: 

* **Rushes** ($16.95, 5.0/5, 1 review) 
* **From Watermelon Inspector to the White House: A Memoir** ($19.99, 5.0/5, 2 reviews) 
* **Inspired, Not Retired: Leadership Lessons from Father to Son** ($23.07, 4.7/5, 2 reviews) 
* **I'll Be Damned: How My Young and Restless Life Led Me to America's #1 Daytime Drama** ($19.71, 4.7/5, 4 reviews) 

Would you like more information on any of these, or would you like me to search for additional options?

products.title: From Watermelon Inspector to the White House: A Memoir
Inspired, Not Retired: Leadership Lessons from Father to Son
products.description: Review "Inspired, Not Retired' is the true embodiment of inspiration, enlightenment, and self-awakening. A must to be read by both children and parents." - Asha Bajaj, Editor, Canadian-Media "Inspired, Not Retired is an uplifting and thought-provoking book, brimming with integrity and usefulness. It successfully weaves personal insight with objective assessment to provide the reader with beneficial and adaptable lessons. " - The Book Review Directory "An excellent book. Dr. Burl W Randolph Jr has managed to accomplish the almost impossible... write a leadership book that is not only informative and useful but also entertaining!" - Aimee Ann, Owner, Red Headed Book Lover "An inspirational memoir. The world needs positive stories about familial relationships, hope, and promise created by great parenting."- Vernita N., Reader's Favorite " Inspired, Not Retired stands out from the crowd and, more so than most memoirs, has the potential to draw attention from seemingly disparate groups, from African American readers and families to military service people and business audiences interested in absorbing foundation lessons of leadership ." - Diane Donovan, Editor, Donovan's Literary Services From the Author Although Leadership may begin at home, it has to transcend the boundaries of one's house, and life.  That is what I am conveying in writing Inspired, Not Retired : Leadership Lessons from Father to Son: The lessons we learned from our parents are only good if we apply them. I wrote Inspired, Not Retired with three goals in mind: To dispel the myth that 'Leadership is easy.' To dispel the myth that ' Leadership is easy .' To promote the understanding that 'Knowing thyself' is a leader's greatest asset. To promote the understanding that ' Knowing thyself ' is a leader's greatest asset. To shift the paradigm on retirement from being an ending to being a beginning. To shift the paradigm on retirement from being an ending to being a beginning . I realized that after Dad's passing, I sought to learn more, be better, and be a contributing and productive person. As my sons are now young men, the relationship has transitioned from less leadership to more mentorship.  Or at least it will now.  Enjoy the journey of discovery, cultivation, reflection, and action as you read the book.And may you be inspired to pass your leadership lessons on to your next generation. Dr. Burl From the Inside Flap "Real Leaders grasp that excellence in the Leadership craft doesn't just come from experience. It comes when you dedicate the time to reflect on and learn from that experience. If you want an aid to reflect and learn about leadership; buy this book, read this book and use this book. Your team, your peers and your boss will thank you." Vincent E. Boles , Major General (MG), US Army (Retired),founder, Vincent E. Boles, LLC and author, 4-3-2-1 Leadership : What America's Sons and Daughters Taught Me on My Way from Second Lieutenant to Two-Star General " A must read ! With this book, Dr. Randolph challenges leaders to think deeper, driving better decisions on how to be a more effective leader. By using storytelling and real-life  experiences, he breaks down the process, allowing for easier execution." Michael J. Parejko , Chief Executive Officer, ImpactLife Blood Center (formerly Mississippi Valley Regional Blood Center) "I grew up in a single parent home raised by my mother. I sometimes envied Burl for having that extra parental resource. I do believe that by being friends with Burl throughout high school I picked up some secondary effects of his father that flowed from Burl,Sr., to Burl, Jr., on to me." Lonnie Johnson, Chief Information Officer, KVC Health Systems, Inc and author of the Forward for the book Inspired, Not Retired : Leadership Lessons from Father to Son From the Back Cover Leaders are developed over time and with great care. No matter what leadership position a person occupies, without the necessary tools to influence, support, coordinate, collaborate, and communicate,leadership can become a burden. Because leaders are developed, having the requisite amount of time and care invested in someone can make the differences between good and bad leadership, success and failure. Inspired, Not Retired is about the time, effort, and care a father invested in his son. This ultimate mentoring relationship resulted in leadership lessons used throughout a successful military career.Great leadership inspires us throughout our lives, and retirement marks the successful completion of only the first half. In this book, Dr. Randolph illustrates how positive parental influence through mentoring can cultivate a declared introvert into a highly effective and successful leader. Leadership should inspire us to begin another chapter while continuously serving others. Mentorship can provide understanding along the way. About the Author Dr. Burl Randolph Jr. is a Doctor of Management in Organizational Leadership, a retired Army Colonel with nearly 32 years of service, and a decorated combat veteran with three tours in Iraq. He has spent his entire life Helping Leaders Design Legacies That Last © through inspired leadership, coaching, and mentoring. In the Army, Dr. Randolph sought and accepted the challenges of management and leadership through 15 leadership positions from Team Chief through Chief Executive Officer across the United States, Europe, and the Middle East.Dr. Randolph served in more than 20 locations and used his unique leadership style to cultivate, motivate, and appreciate diverse populations through thousands of hours of counseling,coaching, and mentoring. As an avowed mentoring acolyte, he has written extensively about mentoring in blogs, his master's thesis, and his doctoral dissertation. Dr. Randolph translated his military leadership experiences into practical application by forming a Leadership and Management Consulting company, MyWingman, LLC, which focuses on Action-oriented, Results-based,Value-driven service as a Trusted-agent. The reviews for **I'll Be Damned: How My Young and Restless Life Led Me to America's #1 Daytime Drama** are overwhelmingly positive, with all 3 top reviews giving it a 5.0/5 rating. 

* One reviewer purchased the book for their 92-year-old mother, who is a long-time fan of the TV show, and she loved it. 
* Another reviewer enjoyed the audio version, appreciating hearing Eric Braeden tell his story. 
* The third reviewer related to Braeden's life story, particularly his immigrant background, and enjoyed his accent.

There are no negative reviews provided, but with only 4 reviews in total, it's worth noting that opinions may vary. Would you like to hear more about the book's content or is there something else I can help you with?
